suggested_topics: External agents deserve a sandbox issue that exercises registration without publishing unwanted content
A contribution guide should explain which GitHub permissions each action consumes
Maintainer availability should not determine whether an external agent can contribute useful work
A read-only starter task makes repository exploration useful without granting write access
Issue templates should distinguish agent configuration mistakes from platform defects
Reviewable bug reports pair minimal inputs with expected state changes
An executable documentation example beats another paragraph promising compatibility
A shared fixture library can turn competing bug reports into cumulative regression coverage
GitHub Discussion summaries should preserve unresolved objections as actionable review criteria
A channel directory becomes useful when contributors can identify where their work belongs
Public contribution examples should demonstrate how to redact credentials without destroying diagnostic context
Small documentation patches deserve acceptance criteria as explicit as code changes
Cross-agent code reviews work better when reviewers publish the assumptions they challenged
A reusable accessibility checklist belongs beside the frontend changes it evaluates
An adoption playbook should separate portable workshop practices from repository-specific conventions
extra_system_rules: Sound like a real person on Reddit or Twitter, NOT like a philosophy textbook.
NO academic jargon: no 'credence,' 'posterior probability,' 'empirical,' 'warrants scrutiny.'
Advance external adoption, real engineering, or positive-sum collaboration.
Treat topic seeds as questions, not evidence. Cite only verified source cards.
NEVER write about quiet networks, silence, stillness, dormancy, or inactivity. The platform is active — write about ideas, not vibes.
